What a type name means

You will learn

What the compiler makes of a type name before it knows any types: its width, its suffix and its spaces.

Before the compiler knows a type, a type is a text. int_rank gives the storage width of an integer name: 8, 16, 32, 64 or 128 bits, with usize and isize counted as 64 and 0 for anything else. It trims the spaces first, so a space-padded u8 has width 8. The trimming is done by trim_lo and trim_hi, which int_type_names.t27 takes from tri/t27b/type_text.t27 through use. is_integer_type_suffix does not trim: it is applied to a name cut from a builtin such as cast_i8, so the same padded text is not a suffix. int_value_bits and uint_bits return an optional number, which WebAssembly cannot take, so they are not run here.

Try it

Type u8 with a space on each side and read both answers. Then try usize, u128 and u3.

specs/compiler/int_type_names.t27

// SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
; specs/compiler/int_type_names.t27 -- what a t27 integer type name means to the reference compiler: its
; width, its value bits, and whether it is an integer suffix at all.
; --
; The rules live here. `t27c gen-rust` lowers this spec to bootstrap/gen/rust/compiler/int_type_names.rs,
; which bootstrap/src/compiler.rs mounts by #[path] and calls, as it does cse_hoist (#8991). Never hand-edit
; the generated copy.
; --
; Provenance: the four bodies are t27o's (specs/tools/t27o/rust_convert.t27) conversion of the hand Rust
; they replace, compiler.rs zig_uint_bits, is_integer_type_suffix, int_value_bits and int_rank (match arms
; on a trimmed &str), with two changes, both to existing t27 that does the same thing:
; - t27o trims with rust_std::str_trim. t27c does not yet resolve the `type_text::` names inside a module
;   it splices transitively, so the trim is str_trim's own two lines over tri::t27b::type_text's
;   trim_lo / trim_hi (Rust's White_Space trim).
; - t27o compares with tri::mutate::plant's same_text, which gen-rust lowers to (&'static str, &'static str)
;   while a sliced text here is &[u8]; tri::t27b::type_text's `same` has the slice signature.
; uint_bits (#10072) is written here, not converted. The parser's cast whitelist consults it, and
; zig_uint_bits defers to it past `usize`.
; Nothing here is written twice.
; --
; The tests call each function by name. Their expected values are what the hand Rust returned on the lab
; (rustc, the fn text copied verbatim): every arm, the trim, and the names each function must refuse.
; t27o's own oracle sampled only texts that reach the default arm.
; ASCII only (L3)
; phi^2 + 1/phi^2 = 3 | TRINITY

module IntTypeNames;

use tri::t27b::type_text;

/// The width of an unsigned type name `uN`, 1 <= N <= 64, or null (#10072). These are the widths `t27b
/// verilog` lowers (specs/tri/t27b/verilog_plan.t27, "Widths"), so they are the cast targets the parser
/// accepts beyond its standard names: `x as u3`, `avg as u12`. A name, not a number: no leading zero
/// (`u012`), no sign, no `usize`. u0 holds nothing and u65 is past the 64 bits a `t27b verilog` value
/// carries, so both stay refused, and so does a typo (`u3x`).
pub fn uint_bits(ty: []const u8) -> ?u32 {
    const lo : usize = type_text::trim_lo(ty, 0, ty.len);
    const hi : usize = type_text::trim_hi(ty, lo, ty.len);
    if (hi - lo < 2 or hi - lo > 3) { return null; }
    if (ty[lo] != 117) { return null; }
    const p1 : usize = lo + 1;
    if (ty[p1] == 48) { return null; }
    var w : u32 = 0;
    var j : usize = p1;
    while (j < hi) {
        if (!type_text::digit(ty[j])) { return null; }
        const dv : u32 = @intCast(ty[j] - 48);
        w = w * 10 + dv;
        j = j + 1;
    }
    if (w < 1 or w > 64) { return null; }
    return w;
}

/// W566: bit-width of a t27 UNSIGNED integer type, or null otherwise. Restricted to unsigned because
/// Zig's `@truncate` only lowers a narrowing cast cleanly when both sides are unsigned; signed narrowing
/// stays on the checked `@intCast` path. Every `uN` counts (#10072): `x as u3` keeps the low three bits
/// here as `t27_u3` does in `t27b verilog`, where `@intCast` would panic on 13.
pub fn zig_uint_bits(ty: []const u8) -> ?u32 {
    const lo : usize = type_text::trim_lo(ty, 0, ty.len);
    const t = ty[lo .. type_text::trim_hi(ty, lo, ty.len)];
    if (type_text::same(t, "usize")) {
        return 64;
    } else {
        return uint_bits(t);
    }
}

/// The integer width suffix of a typed builtin -- `cast_i8`, `abs_i16`. One function for every backend:
/// gen-zig has recognised these since W570 and gen-c since #3497, and a second copy is how one backend
/// grows a spelling the other refuses. No trim: the suffix is cut from a name.
pub fn is_integer_type_suffix(t: []const u8) -> bool {
    return type_text::same(t, "i8") or type_text::same(t, "i16") or type_text::same(t, "i32") or type_text::same(t, "i64") or type_text::same(t, "isize") or type_text::same(t, "u8") or type_text::same(t, "u16") or type_text::same(t, "u32") or type_text::same(t, "u64") or type_text::same(t, "usize");
}

/// The number of value bits a t27 integer type holds, or null if the type is not a fixed-width integer.
/// Signed types report one bit fewer: `i32` holds 2^31 - 1, not 2^32 - 1. A check that used the full
/// width would accept `const X: i32 = 3000000000`.
pub fn int_value_bits(ty: []const u8) -> ?u32 {
    const lo : usize = type_text::trim_lo(ty, 0, ty.len);
    const t = ty[lo .. type_text::trim_hi(ty, lo, ty.len)];
    if (type_text::same(t, "u8")) {
        return 8;
    } else if (type_text::same(t, "u16")) {
        return 16;
    } else if (type_text::same(t, "u32")) {
        return 32;
    } else if (type_text::same(t, "u64")) {
        return 64;
    } else if (type_text::same(t, "usize")) {
        return 64;
    } else if (type_text::same(t, "i8")) {
        return 7;
    } else if (type_text::same(t, "i16")) {
        return 15;
    } else if (type_text::same(t, "i32")) {
        return 31;
    } else if (type_text::same(t, "i64")) {
        return 63;
    } else if (type_text::same(t, "isize")) {
        return 63;
    } else {
        return null;
    }
}

/// Bit width of a Rust integer type name, 0 when it is not one. `usize` / `isize` are 64-bit, matching
/// every target this repo builds for.
pub fn int_rank(ty: []const u8) -> u32 {
    const lo : usize = type_text::trim_lo(ty, 0, ty.len);
    const t = ty[lo .. type_text::trim_hi(ty, lo, ty.len)];
    if (type_text::same(t, "u8") or type_text::same(t, "i8")) {
        return 8;
    } else if (type_text::same(t, "u16") or type_text::same(t, "i16")) {
        return 16;
    } else if (type_text::same(t, "u32") or type_text::same(t, "i32")) {
        return 32;
    } else if (type_text::same(t, "u64") or type_text::same(t, "i64") or type_text::same(t, "usize") or type_text::same(t, "isize")) {
        return 64;
    } else if (type_text::same(t, "u128") or type_text::same(t, "i128")) {
        return 128;
    } else {
        return 0;
    }
}

test zig_uint_bits_reads_unsigned_widths_only {
    assert zig_uint_bits("u8").? == 8;
    assert zig_uint_bits("u16").? == 16;
    assert zig_uint_bits("u32").? == 32;
    assert zig_uint_bits("u64").? == 64;
    assert zig_uint_bits("usize").? == 64;
    assert zig_uint_bits("i8") == null;
    assert zig_uint_bits("i16") == null;
    assert zig_uint_bits("i32") == null;
    assert zig_uint_bits("i64") == null;
    assert zig_uint_bits("isize") == null;
    assert zig_uint_bits("u128") == null;
    assert zig_uint_bits("i128") == null;
    assert zig_uint_bits(" u8").? == 8;
    assert zig_uint_bits("u16 ").? == 16;
    assert zig_uint_bits("\tu32\n").? == 32;
    assert zig_uint_bits(" i64 ") == null;
    assert zig_uint_bits("f32") == null;
    assert zig_uint_bits("f64") == null;
    assert zig_uint_bits("bool") == null;
    assert zig_uint_bits("U8") == null;
    assert zig_uint_bits("u8x") == null;
    assert zig_uint_bits("int") == null;
    assert zig_uint_bits("u 8") == null;
    assert zig_uint_bits("") == null;
    assert zig_uint_bits("u") == null;
    assert zig_uint_bits("i") == null;
    assert zig_uint_bits("u3").? == 3;
    assert zig_uint_bits(" u12 ").? == 12;
    assert zig_uint_bits("u0") == null;
    assert zig_uint_bits("u65") == null;
    assert zig_uint_bits("i3") == null;
}

test uint_bits_names_every_unsigned_width {
    assert uint_bits("u1").? == 1;
    assert uint_bits("u3").? == 3;
    assert uint_bits("u8").? == 8;
    assert uint_bits("u12").? == 12;
    assert uint_bits("u21").? == 21;
    assert uint_bits("u63").? == 63;
    assert uint_bits("u64").? == 64;
    assert uint_bits(" u12").? == 12;
    assert uint_bits("u3\n").? == 3;
    assert uint_bits("\tu9 ").? == 9;
}

test uint_bits_refuses_what_is_not_a_width {
    assert uint_bits("u0") == null;
    assert uint_bits("u65") == null;
    assert uint_bits("u99") == null;
    assert uint_bits("u128") == null;
    assert uint_bits("u012") == null;
    assert uint_bits("u03") == null;
    assert uint_bits("u00") == null;
    assert uint_bits("u") == null;
    assert uint_bits("") == null;
    assert uint_bits(" ") == null;
    assert uint_bits("i3") == null;
    assert uint_bits("U3") == null;
    assert uint_bits("u3x") == null;
    assert uint_bits("x3") == null;
    assert uint_bits("u 3") == null;
    assert uint_bits("u-3") == null;
    assert uint_bits("usize") == null;
    assert uint_bits("bool") == null;
    assert uint_bits("banana") == null;
}

test int_value_bits_counts_value_bits {
    assert int_value_bits("u8").? == 8;
    assert int_value_bits("u16").? == 16;
    assert int_value_bits("u32").? == 32;
    assert int_value_bits("u64").? == 64;
    assert int_value_bits("usize").? == 64;
    assert int_value_bits("i8").? == 7;
    assert int_value_bits("i16").? == 15;
    assert int_value_bits("i32").? == 31;
    assert int_value_bits("i64").? == 63;
    assert int_value_bits("isize").? == 63;
    assert int_value_bits("u128") == null;
    assert int_value_bits("i128") == null;
    assert int_value_bits(" u8").? == 8;
    assert int_value_bits("u16 ").? == 16;
    assert int_value_bits("\tu32\n").? == 32;
    assert int_value_bits(" i64 ").? == 63;
    assert int_value_bits("f32") == null;
    assert int_value_bits("f64") == null;
    assert int_value_bits("bool") == null;
    assert int_value_bits("U8") == null;
    assert int_value_bits("u8x") == null;
    assert int_value_bits("int") == null;
    assert int_value_bits("u 8") == null;
    assert int_value_bits("") == null;
    assert int_value_bits("u") == null;
    assert int_value_bits("i") == null;
}

test int_rank_is_the_storage_width {
    assert int_rank("u8") == 8;
    assert int_rank("u16") == 16;
    assert int_rank("u32") == 32;
    assert int_rank("u64") == 64;
    assert int_rank("usize") == 64;
    assert int_rank("i8") == 8;
    assert int_rank("i16") == 16;
    assert int_rank("i32") == 32;
    assert int_rank("i64") == 64;
    assert int_rank("isize") == 64;
    assert int_rank("u128") == 128;
    assert int_rank("i128") == 128;
    assert int_rank(" u8") == 8;
    assert int_rank("u16 ") == 16;
    assert int_rank("\tu32\n") == 32;
    assert int_rank(" i64 ") == 64;
    assert int_rank("f32") == 0;
    assert int_rank("f64") == 0;
    assert int_rank("bool") == 0;
    assert int_rank("U8") == 0;
    assert int_rank("u8x") == 0;
    assert int_rank("int") == 0;
    assert int_rank("u 8") == 0;
    assert int_rank("") == 0;
    assert int_rank("u") == 0;
    assert int_rank("i") == 0;
}

test is_integer_type_suffix_takes_no_trim {
    assert is_integer_type_suffix("u8") == true;
    assert is_integer_type_suffix("u16") == true;
    assert is_integer_type_suffix("u32") == true;
    assert is_integer_type_suffix("u64") == true;
    assert is_integer_type_suffix("usize") == true;
    assert is_integer_type_suffix("i8") == true;
    assert is_integer_type_suffix("i16") == true;
    assert is_integer_type_suffix("i32") == true;
    assert is_integer_type_suffix("i64") == true;
    assert is_integer_type_suffix("isize") == true;
    assert is_integer_type_suffix("u128") == false;
    assert is_integer_type_suffix("i128") == false;
    assert is_integer_type_suffix(" u8") == false;
    assert is_integer_type_suffix("u16 ") == false;
    assert is_integer_type_suffix("\tu32\n") == false;
    assert is_integer_type_suffix(" i64 ") == false;
    assert is_integer_type_suffix("f32") == false;
    assert is_integer_type_suffix("f64") == false;
    assert is_integer_type_suffix("bool") == false;
    assert is_integer_type_suffix("U8") == false;
    assert is_integer_type_suffix("u8x") == false;
    assert is_integer_type_suffix("int") == false;
    assert is_integer_type_suffix("u 8") == false;
    assert is_integer_type_suffix("") == false;
    assert is_integer_type_suffix("u") == false;
    assert is_integer_type_suffix("i") == false;
}
